doc.title: Gerald Wiggins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 2, 1995

title: Stepin Fetchit job and invitation to join Les Hite for California
summary: Wiggins was working Brooklyn Strand with Stepin Fetchit when Les Hite's band needed a pianist; he describes the comedy act and short weekend tour.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Anyhow, we were working at the Brooklyn Strand and there was a west coast band backing the show by the name of Les Hite. Well the Army took Les Hite’s piano player, and Step had a little problem he had to talk to the police about so he disappeared. So Les said to me, “You don’t have a boss and I don’t have a piano player. How would you like to go to California?” So I was young and crazy I said, “Great.”
And how old were you then?
I must have been just about 18 then. I was just out of high school.
Yeah. It’s so interesting to hear the ages that a lot of folks we’ve talked to have started at. What kind of, just to step back once, what kind of piano playing did you do for Stepin?

Well I was mostly part of his act. I had played some things and I had to help him with a few little things he did like he said, “Help me with this coat” and I put it up to his shoulder and he said, “the hand down there” and I had to drop it down and put it on his hand. It was really, you know, cornball stuff, but it made him a millionaire so what can I say?
Then you traveled around doing little shows?

We didn’t do too—I didn’t stay with him that long. I think we played maybe about four or five weeks. We went as far as Anderson, Indiana and came right back. At that time everything was weekend shows, you know, little towns. Friday and Saturday night was it.
